area: Translation / i18n state of the Solen.ch web app (locale catalogue, language switching, hardcoded copy, DB-side locale columns, CI gates, French register)

corrections.original_claim: The shared DateTimePicker primitive ships German defaults and the HOMEPAGE SEARCH never overrides them. SearchBar.tsx:550-554 renders <DateTimePicker variant="single-date" ... /> with NO `labels` prop, so on /en, /fr, /it the date picker renders "Vormittag / Nachmittag / Abend / Verfügbare Zeiten / Wähle einen Tag / Keine freien Termine / Voriger Monat / Nächster Monat".
corrections.truth: None of those six visible strings render on the homepage search bar. DateTimePicker.tsx:172 defines `const timeColumn = variant === "date-and-time" && (<TimeSlotList .../>)`. Every one of the cited German defaults is consumed only inside TimeSlotList: `labels.availableTimes` at :517, `labels.noSlots`/`labels.pickDay` at :544, `labels.noSlotsHint`/`labels.pickDayHint` at :547, and `labels.morning`/`afternoon`/`evening` at :627-629. SearchBar.tsx:551 passes `variant="single-date"`, so `timeColumn` evaluates to `false` and renders nothing; the component takes the calendar-layout return at DateTimePicker.tsx:231-249, which is SolenCalendar plus `{timeColumn}`. `L.moreDates` (:199, :210) is reachable only from the `dateLayout === "strip"` branch at :186, which the homepage does not use either. The calendar itself is correctly localized: SolenCalendar at :363-369 calls `useLocale()` from next-intl and wraps AriaCalendar in `<I18nProvider locale={locale}>`, so month names and weekday labels render in the active locale. The ONLY German that actually reaches an en/fr/it homepage user here is two aria-labels, `aria-label="Voriger Monat"` at :390 and `aria-label="Nächster Monat"` at :404, which are invisible to sighted users and are hardcoded string literals outside the `labels` object, so the recon's proposed fix (pass a `labels` prop as DateTimeStep.tsx:208 does) would NOT fix them. The prescribed STEP 2 fix is therefore aimed at a non-existent bug.
corrections.evidence: app/[locale]/_components/primitives/DateTimePicker.tsx:172 (`const timeColumn = variant === "date-and-time" && (`), :186 (`if (dateLayout === "strip")`), :203, :231-249, :363-369, :390, :404, :517, :544, :547, :627-629; app/[locale]/_components/homepage/SearchBar.tsx:550-554. The rest of that finding IS confirmed: :542 "Wann?", :560 "Tageszeit", SERVICES literals at :108-117 (recon said 108-116), PERIODS at :126-131 (recon said 126-130), and DateTimeStep.tsx:208 / RescheduleSheet.tsx:216 do pass labels.

corrections.original_claim: 12 read sites hard-code `locale === 'en' ? x_en : x_de`, which means FRENCH AND ITALIAN FALL BACK TO GERMAN, not to English ... Only app/[locale]/inspo/board/[id]/page.tsx:48 handles all four.
corrections.truth: Three separate errors. (a) UNDERCOUNT: the same grep returns 18 lines, not 13. The recon's 12 are all real, but it missed app/[locale]/_components/search/SalonResultCard.tsx:551 and app/[locale]/_components/search/MapSalonDetail.tsx:181 (both `locale === "en" && s.name_en ? s.name_en : s.name_de`) plus app/[locale]/dashboard/bundles/page.tsx:214 and :346. SalonResultCard is the primary search-results card, i.e. a higher-traffic customer surface than several sites the recon did list. (b) DIRECTION WRONG: the blanket 'fr/it fall back to German' is false for the inverted variant, which the recon did not search for. components-legacy/ui/QuickPreviewSheet.tsx:166 `{locale === "de" ? svc.name_de : svc.name_en}` and components-legacy/booking/WaitlistModal.tsx:46 `locale === 'de' ? service.name_de : service.name_en` hand French and Italian users ENGLISH, and with no `?? name_de` guard they render empty when name_en is null. components-legacy/ui/CategoryTree.tsx:61 and app/api/bookings/route.ts:566 are the same inverted shape. (c) 'ONLY inspo/board handles all four' is false: lib/cities.ts:173 `const key = \`name_${locale}\`` (on cities, which has all four columns) is a genuine four-locale reader, as are app/[locale]/_components/salon/SalonAbout.tsx:19-20, app/api/content/route.ts:17, app/[locale]/inspo/[id]/page.tsx:109, app/[locale]/profile/page.tsx:156, components-legacy/booking/BookingCard.tsx:99 and CancelBookingSheet.tsx:67.
corrections.evidence: grep -rn "locale === ['\"]en['\"]" over app/lib/components/components-legacy filtered to lines containing _en or _de returns 18 lines; the inverted `locale === ['\"]de['\"]` grep returns 5 more; the dynamic `name_${locale}` grep returns 11 sites.

corrections.original_claim: The global Header renders 22 hardcoded German page titles on EVERY locale. Header.tsx:409-435 builds a TITLES regex table.
corrections.truth: 20, not 22. The TITLES array is declared at Header.tsx:411 and closes at :437; counting every `[RegExp, string]` entry gives exactly 20: Treueprogramm, Termine, Favoriten, Stempel, Looks, Geschenkkarten, Haarprofil, Gutscheine, Formulare, Freunde einladen, Profil bearbeiten, Einstellungen, Persönliche Angaben, Passwort, Zahlungsmethoden, Sprache, Beauty-Profil, Benachrichtigungen, Konto löschen, Profil. The substance is fully confirmed and I traced it further than the recon did: the value is consumed at :641 and rendered at :649 inside the header bar with no locale branch and no `md:` gate, and the deliberate-choice comment is at :406-408 verbatim.

corrections.original_claim: HARDCODED GERMAN, THE NUMBER: 109 files, 543 occurrences ... Split: 27 files / 95 occurrences are in files that ALREADY call t(), 82 files / 448 occurrences are files with no next-intl call at all.
corrections.truth: The file count reproduces exactly; the occurrence count does not and should not be quoted as a fact. An independent detector over the same tree (comment-stripped, `de:` map branches skipped, JSX text nodes plus labelled string props) returns 109 files and 472 occurrences excluding /dev/, and 121 files / 564 occurrences including it (recon: 119 / 621). The t() split lands at 24 files with t()-plus-German and 85 without (recon: 27 / 82). Occurrence totals from a bespoke German-stopword heuristic are not stable across implementations, so 543 is one detector's output, not a measured property of the repo. The phenomenon and the 109-file scope are real and independently reproduced; the per-file numbers are not.
corrections.evidence: independent scan script at $TMPDIR/de.mjs over 618 .tsx files under app/, components/, components-legacy/

corrections.original_claim: THE 20 WORST FILES BY HARDCODED-GERMAN COUNT: 1. TermsContent.tsx 169; 2. PrivacyContent.tsx 41; ... 8. DateTimePicker.tsx 10 ...
corrections.truth: The ranking's top two are confirmed by an independent scan (TermsContent #1 by a wide margin, PrivacyContent #2) but the counts are not reproducible: I measure 101 and 27, not 169 and 41. DateTimePicker.tsx at rank 8 is also misleading given the correction above: its DEFAULT_LABELS at :79-89 are real German literals, but they only render on the booking and reschedule surfaces, both of which already override them.

corrections.original_claim: i18n adoption by file: 303 .tsx under app/[locale] excluding /dev/, of which 114 import useTranslations/getTranslations. components-legacy: 187 .tsx, 120 use next-intl. components/: 10 .tsx, 0 use next-intl.

corrections.original_claim: [Implicit completeness] The report's enumeration of mixed-language and statutory-risk customer surfaces, and its /terms + /privacy statutory-floor gap.
corrections.truth: The report misses the single clearest statutory-floor case in the estate, which is a stronger instance of the exact argument it makes for /privacy. app/[locale]/_components/primitives/CookieConsent.tsx contains zero calls to useTranslations or getTranslations and renders its entire consent UI in hardcoded German: category descriptions at :405-406 and :415-418, aria-labels "Analyse-Cookies" (:409) and "Marketing-Cookies" (:420), the settings paragraph at :424-431, and the buttons "Abbrechen" (:444) and "Auswahl speichern" (:456). It is not a dormant component: CookieConsentProvider is mounted globally at app/[locale]/layout.tsx:65 and auto-mounts the banner, so it renders on EVERY route in all four locales. A consent banner an Italian or French data subject cannot read is a harder nFADP/GDPR problem than the /privacy text the recon flagged, because consent must be informed to be valid at all. Also worth noting: :427 links to `/datenschutz` with no locale prefix; the route does exist (app/[locale]/datenschutz), but middleware.ts:88-93 will resolve the locale from the NEXT_LOCALE cookie or Accept-Language, so the user can be bounced out of the locale they were reading in.
corrections.evidence: app/[locale]/_components/primitives/CookieConsent.tsx:405-406, :409, :415-420, :424-431, :444, :456; grep -c 'useTranslations|getTranslations' on that file returns 0; app/[locale]/layout.tsx:27, :65, :136-139; middleware.ts:88-93

net_picture:
The recon's central story survives adversarial checking and most of its hard numbers reproduce exactly, but two of its top-priority action items are aimed at the wrong targets and one whole failure mode was missed.

WHAT I REPRODUCED EXACTLY, no caveats (22 of 29 findings). The catalogue is genuinely finished: `node scripts/check-i18n-parity.mjs` prints "check-i18n-parity: OK (5703 keys, all 4 locales in sync)" and exits 0. `node scripts/check-i18n-sentinel.mjs` exits 1 today with four [FAIL] blocks, all on the single legitimate array leaf `dashboard.approvalsPage.checklistItems`, consumed via `t.raw()` at app/[locale]/dashboard/approvals/page.tsx:92; the identical-to-en ratchet passes at its exact baselines (de 466 / fr 368 / it 220), and the `i18n` job at .github/workflows/quality.yml:162-174 runs both scripts with no continue-on-error on push-to-main and every PR, so that job is red on every push. package.json:16 has `check:i18n-parity` and no sentinel script; /Users/sulo/Documents/solen/.git/hooks holds only *.sample.

The switcher diagnosis is correct and is the real complaint. components-legacy/ui/LanguageSwitcher.tsx:46-59 is the only correct implementation (path-segment swap, `document.cookie = NEXT_LOCALE=...` at :55, push + refresh); it is imported in exactly one file, MobileMenu.tsx:21, rendered at :336 as variant="sheet"; its "header"/"menu"/"footer" variants have no render site anywhere. The only thing that can open that sheet is the hamburger at Header.tsx:795, whose className begins `md:hidden` (:802), and MobileMenu mounts at :888 driven solely by that button's state, so on desktop `menuOpen` can never become true and there is no language control at all beyond Footer.tsx:168-177, a bare `<Link href={`/${l.code}`}>` that drops you on the locale homepage and sets no cookie. FooterGate.tsx:24-47 removes even that on /booking, /confirmation, /salon/*/reviews and /salon/*/team. The settings page is a genuine silent no-op: SettingsForm.tsx:92-131 PATCHes /api/profile, toasts, and calls router.refresh() with no cookie write and no navigation, while next-intl reads the locale from the URL segment; the write itself is real (lib/validations.ts:157, app/api/profile/route.ts:71) and profiles.locale is read by well over a dozen email senders, so the control is email-only. The NEXT_LOCALE cookie is near-inert because middleware.ts:9-12 lets the path win and :88-93 only consults the cookie when there is no locale prefix.

The DB finding is exact. Parsing _inventory/_db-columns.json (capturedAt 2026-07-12, 146 tables) yields precisely 15 locale-suffixed column groups, 8 complete and 7 partial, and the 7 partial ones are exactly the customer-content ones the recon named, with the row counts from _db-snapshot.json matching to the row (263 services, 28 salons, 6 service_options, 4 salon_badges, 2 pricing rules, 7 site_content). app/api/salons/route.ts:261 does ILIKE on name_de only while the city resolver 18 lines above at :242-249 matches all four name_* columns, and the route never reads a locale param. app/[locale]/_components/salon/SalonServices.tsx:172 renders `{service.name_de}` unconditionally with a hardcoded "Buchen" at :185 (the recon said :184), mounted on the live PDP via SalonDetailV3.tsx:275 from app/[locale]/salon/[slug]/page.tsx:38. TermsContent.tsx renders German and English together (Section :446-460, Article :462-478, ParDe/ParEn :480-496), contains the string "locale" zero times, and terms/page.tsx:10-13 still advertises fr and it hreflang. The 22 inline four-locale copy-map files reproduce at exactly 22. The French register work is the most impressive part and reproduces to the token once Unicode-correct boundaries are used: formal 436 tokens across 364 keys (vous 149 + votre 241 + vos 46), informal 63 across 51 (tu 13, ton 19, ta 17, tes 6, toi 6, t' 2), zero keys mixing both registers, and the namespace clustering exact (resendAccess 14/0, authRegister 5/0, discoveryFilters 4/0, reviewPrompt 3/0, profileHub 5 informal vs 2 formal, Profile 5 vs 3). German is 22 formal tokens across 15 keys, Italian formal is 0. The catalogue-is-clean claim holds: identical-to-German counts are en 466 / fr 238 / it 179 with only 3/3/1 strings over 25 characters, and my apparent 12 German-marker French hits turned out to be my own regex matching "Terminé" on ASCII \\b, so the recon's zero stands.

WHAT IS WRONG, and it matters for sequencing. Its STEP 2 headline, the homepage DateTimePicker, is a non-bug. `timeColumn` at DateTimePicker.tsx:172 is gated on `variant === "date-and-time"` and the homepage passes `single-date`, so every German string the recon listed is unreachable there; SolenCalendar (:363-369) already calls useLocale() and wraps AriaCalendar in I18nProvider, so months and weekdays localize correctly. The only German left is two aria-labels at :390 and :404, which the proposed `labels` prop cannot reach. Its "12 read sites" is an undercount of 18 that omits SalonResultCard.tsx:551 (the main search-results card) and MapSalonDetail.tsx:181, and its claim that fr/it always fall back to German is contradicted by the inverted pattern it never searched for: QuickPreviewSheet.tsx:166 and WaitlistModal.tsx:46 give fr/it English with no German guard, so they render empty when name_en is null. Its "only one site handles all four" is false; lib/cities.ts:173 and five other dynamic `name_${locale}` readers do. The Header title table is 20 entries, not 22. The 543-occurrence figure is heuristic output, not a repo property, and my independent detector gets 472 from the same 109 files; TermsContent measures 101 and PrivacyContent 27, not 169 and 41. All four catalogue byte sizes are wrong by 32-35 bytes each against a clean git tree.

WHAT IT MISSED. app/[locale]/_components/primitives/CookieConsent.tsx has zero t() calls and is entirely hardcoded German (:405-431, :444, :456), and CookieConsentProvider is mounted globally at app/[locale]/layout.tsx:65, so the consent banner renders in German on every route in all four locales. That is a stronger version of the statutory argument the recon correctly made for /privacy, since consent has to be informed to be valid, and it appears nowhere in the report.

CORRECTED PRIORITY. Step 1 (the switcher) stands unchanged and is still the owner's literal complaint. Step 3 (unblock the red CI job by allowing an array-of-strings leaf at check-i18n-sentinel.mjs:62-73, add the missing npm script) stands. Step 2 should be re-cut: keep SalonServices.tsx:172/:185 and Header.tsx:411-437, drop the DateTimePicker item entirely, and add CookieConsent.tsx and SalonResultCard.tsx:551. Step 4 should target 18 read sites plus the four inverted ones, not 12. The two owner decisions the recon escalated (French vous-vs-tu, and real fr/it legal pages versus dropping the fr/it hreflang) are both correctly raised and both fully evidenced.
